html:
SMTO-GML-0048 — Gmail asked SMTO to slow down

GUID: 5209616c-c185-414e-90ab-19aa3511e4a6
Slug: gmail-rate-limited
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • Gmail limits how many requests an account can make in a short time. SMTO hit that limit, so Gmail turned down this request. Earlier parts of the same Task may already be done.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait at least a few minutes before asking again. If you sent a lot of email today, wait until tomorrow. Gmail lifts short-term limits after a few minutes, but daily sending limits last up to a day.
  2. Open Gmail in your browser and check Sent, Drafts, Trash or your labels to see which changes already went through. Gmail may have finished some of the work before it started refusing requests.
  3. Ask SMTO in the conversation to do only the missing part, in smaller groups, for example 20 emails at a time instead of hundreds. Smaller requests stay under Gmail's limit and avoid sending the same email twice.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the remaining work without this error, and each email or change appears in Gmail only once.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or your Google Cloud project; they can check Gmail's usage limits there. Don't set up rapid repeated retries, and don't resend anything until you've checked Gmail.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gmail API returned 429 (per-user rate or daily quota exceeded), so GmailService._call raised gmail_rate_limited.

What this means

  • The service wrapper maps provider status 429 to its retained Gmail rate-limit kind. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • The service wrapper maps provider status 429 to its retained Gmail rate-limit kind.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect returned wait/quota evidence and any retained write outcome before attempting more requests.

How to fix it

  • Back off before reissuing: wait for the provider's quota window (per-user rate limits recover within minutes; daily sending or API quota may take up to 24 hours), reduce batch size or concurrency, and check Gmail and existing receipts so completed writes are not replayed. Check the Google Cloud console quota page for the OAuth app's project if it recurs.
  • Respect the provider wait period and reduce request volume. Inspect existing mutation receipts before another write.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Request volume and timing respect the actual provider allowance.

What not to do

  • Do not use a rapid retry loop or replay an uncertain mutation while waiting for the stated condition.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
